title: Mining of Switching Sparse Networks for Missing Value Imputation in Multivariate Time Series

problem.claim: Missing values in multivariate time series hinder the application of many analytical methods.

gap.claim: In real-world scenarios, the network structure and the times when the network changes are generally unknown beforehand.

contributions.claim: MissNet imputes missing values in multivariate time series by combining temporal dependency modeling with a state-space model and inter-correlation modeling through switching sparse networks.
The method encodes conditional independence between features in a network to support visual interpretation of relationships relevant to imputation.
The algorithm alternates between inferring networks and filling missing values while discovering network switching, with linear scaling relative to data length.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show MissNet outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms for multivariate time-series imputation.
The authors report that MissNet provides interpretable results.

narrative_sequence.summary: Missing values limit the use of analytical methods on multivariate time series.
Accurate imputation should exploit both temporal dependency and inter-correlation between sequences.
The relevant network may vary over time, while its structure and switching times are unknown in advance.
MissNet combines a state-space model with switching sparse networks, alternately inferring networks and imputing values while discovering network changes.
The authors report improved performance over state-of-the-art methods and interpretable results.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the network-inference procedure.
The abstract does not describe the state-space model or switching mechanism in detail.
The abstract does not provide datasets, evaluation metrics, quantitative results, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
